function.mechanism: Amphiphilic phospholipids reduce oil-water interfacial tension and stabilize emulsions; digestion releases choline-containing metabolites.
common_food_categories: Foods for special medical purposes (EU FC 13.1.5.1)

adi.basis: EFSA 2017 concluded there was no need for a numerical ADI for lecithins (E 322); 2020 follow-up found no safety concerns up to MPL for infants below 16 weeks in assessed categories.

efsa.key_finding: No safety concern was identified at refined exposure estimates in the 2017 re-evaluation, and no safety concern up to MPL for infants below 16 weeks in the 2020 follow-up.

fda.notes: Part 184 is the GRAS-affirmed framework; lecithin and enzyme-modified lecithin are used under current good manufacturing practice. Related modified lecithin rule: 21 CFR 172.814 (hydroxylated lecithin).

adi.basis: JECFA entry for LECITHIN, partially hydrolyzed (ID 1478) does not display a separate ADI statement; parent LECITHIN entry (ID 1477) has ADI 'NOT LIMITED'.

concerns.summary: Residual soy/egg proteins in lecithins can trigger reactions in sensitive individuals; EFSA noted residual proteins should be reduced as much as possible.
Potential neurodevelopment concern in very young infants was specifically reviewed by EFSA in 2020 and not confirmed as a safety issue up to MPL.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017: no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at refined exposure estimates.
EFSA 2020: no safety concerns up to MPL in infant formula/FSMP uses for infants below 16 weeks.
JECFA parent lecithin entry lists ADI as NOT LIMITED.

populations: Not directly applicable because EFSA did not set a numerical ADI for E322 and JECFA parent lecithin ADI is not limited
Allergy-susceptible soy/egg-sensitive individuals remain a practical concern
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA refined exposure estimates are available, but classic ADI exceedance calculation is not applicable for this additive group due absence of a numeric ADI.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evaluations from EFSA and JECFA do not indicate a broad population safety concern at assessed uses, and US CFR places lecithin forms in GRAS/approved frameworks under GMP. The main residual risk is allergenicity from trace proteins in sensitive individuals.
key_factors: EFSA 2017: no numerical ADI needed and no safety concern in assessed populations
EFSA 2020: infant-below-16-weeks follow-up did not identify safety concerns up to MPL
eCFR Part 184 GRAS framework includes lecithin and enzyme-modified lecithin
JECFA parent lecithin ADI is not limited; partial hydrolyzed entry exists with no separate ADI text
No IARC monograph classification found for lecithin in current IARC classification feed
Residual allergen risk remains for soy/egg-sensitive individuals
